subject: SR-71 Blackbird
fact: Its titanium came largely from the USSR via shell companies
detail: The CIA secretly bought Soviet titanium to build a plane meant to spy on the USSR

subject: Concorde
fact: It flew at Mach 2 and the airframe stretched ~20cm from the heat
detail: Cruising friction heated the fuselage enough to visibly lengthen it in flight

subject: Boeing 747
fact: The upper deck exists because Boeing thought jets would be replaced by SSTs
detail: The hump let the nose open for cargo once passenger 747s became obsolete (they didn't)

subject: Gimli Glider
fact: An Air Canada 767 ran out of fuel at 41000 ft and glided to a safe landing
detail: A metric conversion error left it dry mid-flight; the crew deadstick-landed on a drag strip

subject: GE90
fact: The GE90-115B fan blades are so big the engine is wider than a 737 fuselage
detail: It holds the record for highest thrust of any jet engine

subject: An-225 Mriya
fact: It had six engines and was the heaviest aircraft ever built
detail: Only one was ever completed; it could carry 250 tonnes

subject: Ground effect
fact: Airliners "float" just before touchdown because a cushion of air forms under the wing
detail: The trapped air between wing and runway briefly increases lift

subject: Contrails
fact: Contrails are clouds made of ice crystals forming on jet exhaust
detail: They only form when the upper air is cold and humid enough
